transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hello, doctor. Well, I came in because... I seem to be spending far too much of my day just opening the same folders and drawers. And labeled boxes, too. I keep opening them again and again to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. It's very frustrating, because I do this even when I've just checked them a few minutes before. I just can't seem to stop checking.
What goes through your mind, or what do you worry might happen, if you don't check?

Well, it's this nagging thought that just won't leave me alone. Even when I know better, a thought will keep needling me that... that I might have accidentally thrown away my late husband's old tax papers, or maybe I put a precious family recipe in the wrong box. And if I don't go check, I just can't seem to let it pass. I start feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and the only way to make that feeling go away is to open the drawer and look.
Besides these concerns about misplacing or throwing away important items, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday matters, such as your health, finances, or family?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I keep an eye on my health, naturally, but I don't fret over it constantly. My finances are all settled, and my family is doing perfectly fine. 

It really is just... just this business with my papers and the boxes. That's the only thing that consumes my mind and gets me so worked up. I don't really sit around worrying about those other everyday matters.
